construct: signal-peptide-less cEnc with native N-terminal diheme cytochrome domain
condition:
recombinant WT cEnc expressed anaerobically in 
E. coli BL21(DE3) Star; native N-terminal signal peptide omitted; cargo-free shell characterization
notes:
Canonical recombinant WT T=3 cEnc assembly. Giessen & Silver 2017 placed the K. stuttgartiensis shell in the T=3 class 
and measured 33 nm particles by negative-stain TEM. The N-terminal diheme cytochrome domain is a native fusion and is therefore part of the WT shell protein rather than an engineered modification. The experimental construct omitted the predicted 36-residue N-terminal signal peptide. When the isolated NIR domain of the cognate NIR-HAO protein was coexpressed, ~30 NIR copies co-purified per 180-mer capsid, but this truncated cargo-loading condition did not demonstrate a distinct global shell architecture and is not treated as a separate assembly.
